See also: строи and строј

Bulgarian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [strɔj]
  • Audio (Standard Bulgarian):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɔj

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *strojь.

Noun

[edit]

строй • (stroj) m

  1. formation, order, array (manner of arranging a military unit or a large group of people)
    разгъ́нат строй
    razgǎ́nat stroj
    deployed formation
    под строй
    pod stroj
    in formation
  2. column, line, rank, file (of lined-up soldiers, students, etc.)
    отби́ се от стро́я
    otbí se ot strója
    [he] stepped out of the line
  3. ranks, active duty (active military unit)
    връ́щам се в стро́я
    vrǎ́štam se v strója
    to return to active duty
  4. system, order (system of social, economic, or state organization)
    социалисти́чески строй
    socialistíčeski stroj
    socialist system
    робовладе́лчески строй
    robovladélčeski stroj
    slave-owning system
    икономи́чески строй
    ikonomíčeski stroj
    economic system
  5. (music) tuning, pitch (relationship of the tones of a musical instrument by pitch)
    кита́ра с испа́нски строй
    kitára s ispánski stroj
    guitar with Spanish tuning
  6. (rare, figurative) structure, makeup, constitution, essence
    душе́вен строй
    dušéven stroj
    spiritual makeup / mindset
    стро́ят на ми́слене
    strójat na míslene
    the structure of thinking

Derived terms

[edit]
  • вли́зам в стро́я (vlízam v strója) / вля́за в стро́я (vljáza v strója, “to become operational; to enter service; to get to work”)
  • изли́зам от стро́я (izlízam ot strója) / изля́за от стро́я (izljáza ot strója, “to go out of action; to break down; to become incapacitated”)

Related terms

[edit]
  • строя́ (strojá)
  • строе́ж (stroéž)
  • устро́йство (ustrójstvo)

Etymology 2

[edit]

See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

Verb

[edit]

строй • (stroj)

  1. second-person singular imperative of строя́ (strojá)

Russian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [stroj]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Saint Petersburg):(file)

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Old East Slavic строи (stroi), from Proto-Slavic *strojь. Cognate to Russian строить (stroitʹ, “to build, construct”).

Noun

[edit]

строй • (stroj) m inan (genitive стро́я, nominative plural стро́и, genitive plural стро́ев)

  1. system, structure
    социа́льный стро́й ― sociálʹnyj strój ― social structure/system
    метри́ческий стро́й ― metríčeskij strój ― metrical structure
    экономи́ческий стро́й ― ekonomíčeskij strój ― economic system
  2. (music) tuning
    равноме́рно темпери́рованный стро́й ― ravnomérno temperírovannyj strój ― equal-tempered tuning

Noun

[edit]

строй • (stroj) m inan (genitive стро́я, nominative plural строи́, genitive plural строёв)

  1. row, line (of books, bottles, etc. arranged in sequence)
  2. (military) rank, row (of soldiers, tanks, etc.)
  3. (military) formation (of soldiers, tanks, etc.)
    в строю́ ― v strojú ― in formation

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

строй • (stroj)

  1. second-person singular imperative imperfective of стро́ить (stróitʹ)

Related terms

[edit]

  • строи́тельный (stroítelʹnyj), стро́йный (strójnyj)
  • строи́ть (stroítʹ)
